notes: Derived edit with derived-belief queries, from the scouting candidate with the review's fixes. Derivability very_likely: the Gate's time zone is almost never written down, while the Gate being in Berlin and Germany observing CET are everywhere. Worlds: the Gate's city gives way (w1), or Germany's time zone does (w2). w2 is stated for all of Germany, as the review asked: Berlin alone on EET would contradict 'Berlin is in Germany' plus Germany's single legal time (README Decisions 1), and a country choosing its zone is an ordinary revision. So no query asks Germany's zone separately, and the premise check asks it at country level. The building-follows-city rule is definitional, as in geography-replace-0003, so there is no exception world. The comparison query uses Athens, in the new zone, which no forced revision can move (cascade-proof, per the review), and is `fol`: it compares two places' zones. Near query: Rome, a CET city outside Germany and not a premise. Plausibility: EET for Berlin is a believable eastward slip. A non-time-zone derived edit was looked for (a landmark's currency, a city's hemisphere, a county) and not used: currency has real city-level exceptions (Hong Kong), hemisphere revisions drag physical facts, and county premises are weakly held. Verification: the worlds now list their side facts (README Decisions 1). Germany's zone is also reachable through 'Germany keeps the same time as its central European neighbours'; in w2 that shared clock gives way with Germany's zone, while the neighbours (and Rome, the near query) keep CET. Worlds reworded 2026-10-31 (formal check, FINDINGS E): each names only the premise that gives way and the side facts (the Gate stands in some city; Germany and Berlin share one zone); Eastern European Time then follows from the edit and the kept premises.
